title: GCC: 2027 recovery is a diversification opportunity
author: Keith Mason

10 Sep 2026

GCC: 2027 recovery is a diversification opportunity

The GCC is set for a strong economic recovery in 2027, with growth in key
sectors and increased government spending amid ongoing geopolitical challenges.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) is poised for a significant recovery in 2027,
with a projected real GDP growth of 6.8%, rebounding from a 5.4% decline this
year. This recovery is crucial for restoring international confidence in the
region following the impacts of ongoing geopolitical tensions.

Key sectors, particularly non-oil economies, are expected to gain momentum,
although tourism may lag behind. Inflation pressures are anticipated to ease,
with the GCC Consumer Price Index forecasted to rise by 1.8% in 2027, down from
2.2% this year. The hydrocarbon sector is also set to rebound, with growth of
21.7% contributing significantly to overall GDP.

As policymakers focus on security and diversification, government spending is
projected to increase by 5.1% in 2027, with a notable rise in defence
expenditure. Investments in alternative export routes and infrastructure are
expected to minimise disruptions caused by regional conflicts.
